profile.reading: This is a Cogent Communications data center in Phoenix, Arizona, part of Cogent Communications Holdings network, though no source checked this session disclosed a specific street address, power capacity, or square footage for this particular Phoenix building, an honest gap this registry records rather than estimates. Cogent Communications was founded in 1999 by David Schaeffer, who remains chief executive, launching at the height of the dot-com era with backing from angel investors including members of Keiretsu Forum, and is headquartered in Washington, D.C. Within its first three years the company pursued an aggressive acquisition strategy, reportedly acquiring 13 failing telecommunications carriers and purchasing about 14 billion dollars in capital assets, including roughly 4 billion dollars in property, plant, and equipment, for a combined 60 million dollars between 2001 and 2004, including the major United States assets of PSINet and the LambdaNet operations in France and Spain. Cogent operates a large scale internet backbone network carrying more than 100 terabits per second of traffic under its own Autonomous System Number 174, reported about 1,947 employees and 940.9 million dollars in revenue as of 2023, and offers colocation services within data centers as part of its broader network and hosting business, of which this Phoenix facility is one location.
profile.research_note: Cogent's own site confirms the Phoenix office/PoP address (3410 E. University Dr Suite 350, Phoenix AZ 85034) but Cogent does not publish IT capacity, sqft, or certification figures for its network PoP/colocation sites.
sources_tried: Reverse geocoding this rows own coordinates through a third party service (single, uncorroborated 0.9 confidence result, declined per this projects confidence versus corroboration standard), the operators own Phoenix office listing page (different address, described as an office, not confirmed as this facility), a dedicated aggregator listing attempt (not found), a Wikipedia check (no Phoenix facility mentioned), and a data center area directory listing (page not found)

reading.body:
Cogent Communications operates a colocation point of presence in Phoenix at a published address, but does not disclose the IT capacity, square footage, or power draw of this facility on its website. No technical specifications are available to assess whether this site hosts significant AI infrastructure or remains a general-purpose network hub.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 operators publish power capacity figures totaling 512 MW. This Cogent Phoenix location is not among the four with published specifications, placing it outside the ranked set entirely. The absence of a published figure means it cannot be evaluated against the state's known capacity.

Without disclosed power, rack count, or facility certifications, this campus cannot be read as a meaningful data point in AI infrastructure scaling. Cogent's network backbone role and colocation business suggest technical competence, but the operator's choice not to publish capacity means this site's relevance to the grid constraint on AI compute remains unknown.
